docs.title: LongProbe
docs.text: Sub-second RAG regression testing for production pipelines

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
"Did my last commit break retrieval?" — now you know in seconds.

LongProbe is a sub-second RAG regression harness. Define your Golden Questions once, run longprobe check on every commit, and get an exact diff of which document chunks were lost in your latest change — before your users notice.

Think pytest --watch for your RAG pipeline.

docs.title: Why LongProbe?
docs.text:
Every RAG developer faces the same silent killer: you refactor chunking strategy, upgrade LangChain, or add a new document — and your retrieval silently degrades. DeepEval and RAGChecker are heavyweight evaluation frameworks meant for batch analysis, not fast regression checks in a dev loop.

LongProbe gives you instant feedback:

  • ⚡ Sub-second checks on small golden sets
  • 🔍 Exact diffs showing which chunks were lost/gained
  • 📊 Recall scores with per-question breakdown
  • 💾 Baseline tracking to catch regressions over time
  • 🧪 pytest integration for existing test suites
  • 🔌 Pluggable adapters for any vector store

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Install
pip install longprobe

# Initialize
longprobe init

# Define your golden questions in goldens.yaml
# Configure your vector store in longprobe.yaml

# Run checks
longprobe check

# Save baseline
longprobe baseline save --label v1.0

# Compare after changes
longprobe diff --baseline v1.0

docs.title: Complete Workflow
docs.text: Full RAG regression testing workflow from auto-capture to regression detection.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This demo demonstrates the complete LongProbe workflow in action. Perfect for:

  • ✅ Understanding how LongProbe works end-to-end
  • ✅ First-time users learning the tool
  • ✅ Seeing all features in one comprehensive demo
  • ✅ Understanding the regression detection process

docs.title: 1. Test Questions
docs.text:
Shows the questions being tested upfront:

  • Sample questions from your golden set
  • Clear visibility into what's being validated
  • Understanding the scope of testing

docs.title: 2. Workflow Progress (Animated)
docs.text:
A single, continuously updating progress panel showing:

  • Step 1: Start Mock RAG API - Simulates your RAG backend
  • Step 2: Build Golden Set - Auto-capture questions and expected chunks
  • Step 3: Run Initial Check - Test retrieval quality (100% pass)
  • Step 4: Save Baseline - Store results for future comparison
  • Step 5: Break API - Simulate a regression (remove a document)
  • Step 6: Detect Regression - Catch the issue automatically

docs.title: 3. Retrieval Example
docs.text:
Shows what the API returns:

  • Actual question being tested
  • Retrieved chunks with similarity scores
  • Understanding how retrieval works

docs.title: 4. Regression Detection
docs.text:
Shows exactly what broke:

  • Which question failed
  • What chunk went missing
  • Clear explanation of the regression

docs.title: 5. Results Table
docs.text:
Provides before/after comparison:

  • Overall recall (100% → 86.7%)
  • Pass rate (100% → 60%)
  • Number of failed tests (0 → 2)

docs.title: Use Case
docs.text:
Scenario: You're building a RAG application and want to ensure changes don't break retrieval quality.

Workflow:

  1. Capture baseline - Auto-generate golden questions from your RAG API
  2. Run tests - Verify everything works (100% pass)
  3. Save baseline - Store the perfect state
  4. Make changes - Refactor, upgrade, or modify your RAG pipeline
  5. Detect regressions - LongProbe catches issues automatically
  6. Fix and verify - Address issues and re-run tests

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
The demo script shows the complete workflow:

from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import HttpAdapter
from longprobe.core.golden import GoldenSet, GoldenQuestion

# 1. Configure HTTP adapter for your RAG API
adapter = HttpAdapter(config=http_config)

# 2. Auto-capture golden questions
golden_questions = []
for question_text, tags in test_questions:
    results = adapter.retrieve(query=question_text, top_k=3)
    required_chunks = [r["text"] for r in results]
    golden_questions.append(GoldenQuestion(
        question=question_text,
        required_chunks=required_chunks,
        tags=tags
    ))

golden_set = GoldenSet(questions=golden_questions)
golden_set.to_yaml("goldens.yaml")

# 3. Run initial check
probe = LongProbe(adapter=adapter, goldens_path="goldens.yaml")
report = probe.run()
print(f"Recall: {report.overall_recall:.1%}")

# 4. Save baseline
probe.save_baseline(label="latest")

# 5. After making changes...
report_after = probe.run()

# 6. Detect regression
diff = probe.diff(baseline_label="latest")
if diff["regressions"]:
    print(f"⚠️  {len(diff['regressions'])} regressions detected!")

docs.title: Key Features Demonstrated
docs.text:
• 🎯 Auto-capture - Generate golden questions from your API
  • 📊 Live progress - Single animated workflow panel
  • 🔍 Retrieval visibility - See what chunks are retrieved
  • 💾 Baseline tracking - Save and compare results
  • 🚨 Regression detection - Catch issues automatically
  • 📈 Before/after comparison - Clear metrics on what changed

docs.title: Step 1: Start Mock RAG API
docs.text: Simulates your RAG backend with a simple HTTP server. In production, this would be your actual RAG API (LongTrainer, LangServe, etc.).

docs.title: Step 2: Build Golden Set
docs.text: Auto-captures golden questions by querying your API and saving the retrieved chunks as expected results. This is the "capture" workflow.

docs.title: Step 3: Run Initial Check
docs.text: Tests all questions against your RAG API and verifies 100% recall. This establishes your baseline.

docs.title: Step 4: Save Baseline
docs.text: Stores the perfect state in SQLite for future comparison. You can have multiple baselines (v1.0, v2.0, etc.).

docs.title: Step 5: Break API
docs.text: Simulates a regression by removing a document. In real scenarios, this could be: - Refactoring chunking strategy - Upgrading embedding model - Changing retrieval parameters - Accidentally deleting documents

docs.title: Step 6: Detect Regression
docs.text: Re-runs tests and compares against baseline. LongProbe automatically detects: - Which questions failed - What chunks went missing - Exact recall delta

docs.text:

  • Confidence before deployment

docs.title: Detect RAG Regressions Over Time
docs.text: The Detect Regressions demonstration shows how to establish a baseline snapshot of your RAG pipeline and automatically detect retrieval regressions whenever chunking, embeddings, or documents change.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A retrieval regression occurs when a modification to your RAG pipeline (such as changing chunk_size, updating vector database indexes, or removing documents) causes the vector store to fail to retrieve ground-truth chunks that previously succeeded.

LongProbe's baseline tracking allows you to save named baselines (e.g. production-v1), run tests after making changes, and generate detailed regression reports highlighting exact lost chunks.

docs.title: Running the Demo
docs.text:
To run the regression detection demo locally:

uv run python demo_run/detect_regressions.py

docs.title: Two-Step Baseline Comparison Workflow
docs.text:
The regression detection workflow consists of two core steps:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant LP as LongProbe
    participant Store as Baseline Store

    Dev->>LP: Step 1: Run & Save Baseline
    LP->>Store: Save baseline ("production")
    Dev->>LP: Pipeline Update (Chunking/Embedding Change)
    Dev->>LP: Step 2: Run Check & Compare
    LP->>Store: Compare current run vs "production"
    LP-->>Dev: Alert: Display missing chunks & recall delta (Δ)

docs.title: Code Example: Saving & Comparing Baselines
docs.text:
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.core.baseline import BaselineStore

# 1. Initialize LongProbe
probe = LongProbe(adapter=adapter, goldens_path="goldens.yaml")

# 2. Run initial check & save production baseline
initial_report = probe.run()
probe.save_baseline(label="production-v1")

# --- Developer updates RAG pipeline or re-indexes documents ---

# 3. Run check on updated pipeline
new_report = probe.run()

# 4. Compare current run against baseline
baseline_store = BaselineStore(db_path=".longprobe/baselines.db")
baseline_report = baseline_store.load("production-v1")

diff = baseline_store.diff(new_report, baseline_report)

# 5. Check for regressions
if diff.get("regressions"):
    print("⚠️ REGRESSIONS DETECTED!")
    for reg in diff["regressions"]:
        print(f"Question: {reg['question_id']}")
        print(f"Recall Drop: {reg['baseline_recall']:.1%} -> {reg['current_recall']:.1%}")
        print(f"Lost Chunks: {reg['lost_chunks']}")
else:
    print("✅ No regressions detected - safe to deploy!")

docs.title: Command Line Interface (CLI) Baseline Workflow
docs.text:
You can manage baselines directly from your terminal:

# Save baseline snapshot
uv run longprobe baseline save --label production-v1

# List all saved baselines
uv run longprobe baseline list

# Compare current pipeline against saved baseline
uv run longprobe baseline diff production-v1

docs.title: Monitor RAG Quality Demo
docs.text: The Monitor RAG Quality demonstration illustrates how to continuously measure RAG retrieval performance against saved Golden Questions using LongProbe.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In production RAG systems, monitoring retrieval quality is critical to ensure that changes to documents, embeddings, or vector databases do not silently degrade recall.

This demo connects LongProbe to a vector store (ChromaDB), evaluates a set of approved golden questions, and renders an interactive Rich TUI table displaying recall scores, pass/fail status, and retrieved chunk counts.

docs.title: Running the Demo
docs.text:
To run the RAG quality monitoring demo locally:

uv run python demo_run/monitor_rag_quality.py

docs.title: Interactive TUI Output
docs.text:
When executed, LongProbe performs three live setup and evaluation phases:

  1. Setup: Connects to the vector store and seeds/loads sample documents.
  2. Loading: Loads approved golden questions from goldens.yaml.
  3. Testing: Queries the vector store for each question and calculates recall.

docs.title: How It Works Under the Hood
docs.text:
import os
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import create_adapter

# 1. Connect to vector database adapter
adapter = create_adapter(
    "chroma",
    collection_name="demo_collection",
    persist_directory="./.demo_chroma_db"
)

# 2. Initialize LongProbe with Golden Questions
probe = LongProbe(
    adapter=adapter,
    goldens_path="goldens.yaml"
)

# 3. Execute quality check
report = probe.run()

# 4. Inspect results
print(f"Overall Recall: {report.overall_recall:.1%}")
for result in report.results:
    print(f"Question: {result.question_id} -> Recall: {result.recall_score:.1%}")

docs.title: Quality Threshold Enforcement
docs.text:
You can enforce hard quality gates in Python or CLI:

uv run longprobe check --goldens goldens.yaml --threshold 0.85

If overall recall falls below 85%, LongProbe outputs a quality warning diagnostic panel and exits with status code 1, preventing deployment of broken RAG pipelines.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: goldens.yaml defines what to test: questions, expected chunks, match mode, tags, approval status, and per-question top_k. longprobe.yaml defines connections, scoring, baselines, and generation settings.

docs.title: Working retrieval configuration
docs.text:
retriever:
  type: http
  http:
    url: http://localhost:8000/api/retrieve
    method: POST
    body_template: '{"query": "{question}", "top_k": {top_k}}'
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer ${API_TOKEN}
    response_mapping:
      results_path: data.chunks
      id_field: chunk_id
      text_field: content
      score_field: similarity
    timeout: 30
scoring:
  recall_threshold: 0.8
  fail_on_regression: true
baseline:
  db_path: .longprobe/baselines.db
  auto_compare: true

Remove the Authorization header when your local endpoint does not require authentication. HTTP settings live under retriever.http. Chroma/Pinecone/Qdrant connection fields live directly under retriever:

retriever:
  type: chroma
  collection: documents
  persist_directory: ./chroma_db

Pinecone uses index_name, api_key, and namespace. Qdrant uses collection, host, port, and optional api_key. Their normal text-question flow is not connected to query embeddings in v0.1.3; use a properly configured application HTTP endpoint or custom Python adapter until that integration is implemented. Framework retrievers require the Python API.

docs.title: Strict loading and accepted values
docs.text:
CLI commands that accept a configuration path require that selected file to exist and be valid. Invalid files never silently become default settings. init, edit, and help need no retriever configuration. Baseline list/delete use their existing --db-path option rather than reading longprobe.yaml.

Python callers supplying an adapter may omit the conventional longprobe.yaml; documented defaults are then used. ./longprobe.yaml has the same behavior. Missing custom/absolute selected paths raise FileNotFoundError. Any existing invalid selected file fails.

  • Supplied sections and nested HTTP settings must be mappings.
  • Omitted optional fields keep defaults; explicit invalid or null values fail.
  • Integer fields accept integers or integer strings; booleans and fractional values are invalid.
  • Floats must be finite. Recall threshold must be between 0 and 1.
  • Ports must be 1–65535, dimensions nonnegative, and timeouts/batch sizes/generation counts/token limits positive.
  • Booleans accept YAML booleans or case-insensitive strings true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off.
  • Provider-specific extra mappings are preserved; this patch does not redesign unknown-key handling.

Validation errors identify fields without printing their values. Correct misspelled or incorrectly nested known settings; extra fields are not automatically used by every CLI adapter.

docs.title: Environment variables and active providers
docs.text:
${VARIABLE} values are expanded recursively. Unresolved placeholders in fields used by the current operation fail before its service calls. Unused generator/embedder credential placeholders do not block unrelated retrieval checks. Supplied typed numeric/structure settings are still validated even in inactive sections.

Generator configuration example:

generator:
  provider: ollama
  model: your-installed-model
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
  num_questions: 20
  temperature: 0.7
  max_tokens: 4096

Cloud generation may use generator.api_key or the provider environment variable, such as OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or GEMINI_API_KEY. Changing a generator model affects generated questions, not checks against existing goldens. Auto-capture validates both generator and retriever settings before generation. Local Chroma, unauthenticated Qdrant, and Ollama do not require unrelated cloud credentials.

docs.title: Scoring and baselines
docs.text:
recall_threshold controls per-question pass/fail. fail_on_regression: true makes check exit unsuccessfully for a failed question or detected question-level baseline recall decrease. Setting it to false does not suppress configuration or empty-suite failures.

baseline.db_path selects SQLite storage. auto_compare compares with the literal label latest, if it exists. CI must restore this database explicitly when historical comparison is needed. No baseline schema migration is introduced.

docs.title: Embedding and matching limitations
docs.text:
The standalone QueryEmbedder utility supports provider/model/dimensions/batch-size settings, but normal check and LongProbe.run() do not invoke it. Local test mode produces zero vectors, not useful semantic embeddings. Changing only embedder.model does not change normal retrieval.

match_mode: semantic uses word-frequency cosine similarity. Its threshold belongs to each golden question and does not use QueryEmbedder.

docs.title: Safe files
docs.text:
Golden saves, initialized configuration files, and generated question exports use a same-directory temporary file, flush, and atomic replacement. Existing restrictions are preserved; read-only or symbolic-link replacement targets are rejected. Recoverable failures preserve original destination bytes. The guarantee is per file for a single writer, not a multi-file transaction or concurrent-write solution.

init preserves existing files unless --force is specified. Auto-capture always requires a valid existing golden file and merges new drafts. Question-list export requires --overwrite to replace an existing --output file. Back up important files before upgrading or making deliberate replacements.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: LongProbe tests whether your retriever still returns expected evidence for a fixed set of questions. It does not automatically inspect every live user query.

docs.title: 1. Install and initialize
docs.text:
pip install longprobe
longprobe init

Initialization creates two example files and a baseline directory:

  • goldens.yaml: questions and required evidence.
  • longprobe.yaml: retrieval connection, scoring, and baseline settings.
  • .longprobe/: local baseline storage.

The file content comes from GOLDENS_TEMPLATE and CONFIG_TEMPLATE strings in CLI source. init does not read documents, embeddings, or a database. Existing files are preserved unless you explicitly run longprobe init --force.

docs.title: 2. Configure a retriever
docs.text:
You need an existing retrieval endpoint or supported store. For a synthetic local example, run this command from a source checkout in another terminal:

python examples/http_retriever.py

This development fixture returns a known refund-policy chunk; it is not a production retrieval service. Configure longprobe.yaml:

retriever:
  type: http
  http:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve
    method: POST
    response_mapping:
      results_path: data.chunks
      id_field: chunk_id
      text_field: content
      score_field: similarity

scoring:
  recall_threshold: 0.8
  fail_on_regression: true

baseline:
  db_path: .longprobe/baselines.db
  auto_compare: true

For Chroma, install longprobe[chroma] and configure collection and persist_directory directly under retriever, not under a nested chroma section. The application/store handles its existing embedding model; the embedder configuration is not connected to the normal check path in this release.

docs.title: 3. Define verified golden questions
docs.text:
Replace the sample cases in goldens.yaml with requirements you have verified:

name: refund-policy
version: "1.0"
questions:
  - id: refund_policy
    question: What is the refund policy?
    required_chunks:
      - Refunds are allowed within 30 days.
    match_mode: text
    top_k: 5
    status: approved
    tags: [policy, critical]

Alternatively, capture a question through your configured retriever:

longprobe capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto
longprobe edit

Automatic capture saves drafts. In the editor, review the evidence in YAML as necessary, approve the intended drafts, and save. Interactive capture lets you select evidence and saves approved questions. Do not assume current retrieval output is independently correct ground truth.

For document-based generation, install longprobe[generate], configure your generator provider/model and credentials, then run:

longprobe generate ./documents --num-questions 20 --auto-capture
longprobe edit

PDF/Word extraction depends on installed parsing capabilities. Generating questions without --auto-capture produces a question list rather than a complete evaluable golden set. The terminal editor currently edits question text, status, and mode; use YAML to review/change required evidence.

docs.title: 4. Check and save a baseline
docs.text:
longprobe check
longprobe baseline save --label latest

Every approved question is sent to the retriever. LongProbe matches the returned evidence, calculates recall, and applies the passing threshold. With fail_on_regression: true, a below-threshold question or detected baseline regression makes check fail.

latest is a literal baseline label. Saving a different label does not update it. Baseline-save quality policy is unchanged in this patch: the CLI checks overall recall, while the Python save API has no equivalent quality gate.

After changing your retrieval pipeline:

longprobe check
longprobe diff --baseline latest

docs.title: 5. Recover from input failures
docs.text:
Failure Action Missing CLI configuration Run init and configure it, or pass --config PATH Invalid YAML or value Correct the reported field/syntax; LongProbe will not silently use defaults Unresolved active credential Set the named environment variable or fix the active provider setting No matching/approved questions Correct tags, add questions, or review and approve drafts Invalid existing goldens during generation Repair the file or choose a new --goldens PATH; trusted data is not reset Existing question-list export Choose a new output path or explicitly use --output PATH --overwrite

Empty suites may be created/edited, but cannot pass evaluation. --include-drafts includes actual drafts, not an empty-suite bypass.

docs.title: Other entry points
docs.text:
longprobe check --output github
longprobe check --tag critical
longprobe watch

Watch polls the golden file and runs after a change; it does not initially run or watch configuration/remote index changes. Configuration edits take effect the next time a check is invoked.

See configuration, CLI reference, and v0.1.3 release notes for limits and compatibility changes.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Use longprobe COMMAND --help for all implemented options. Unless overridden, golden/config paths are goldens.yaml and longprobe.yaml.

Command Purpose init Create example files; preserve existing files unless --force check Evaluate selected approved questions against the configured retriever capture Query supplied questions and select evidence; --auto creates drafts generate PATH Generate questions from document text edit Review statuses, edit question text/mode, approve drafts, and save baseline save Evaluate approved questions and save a labeled snapshot subject to the existing overall-recall gate baseline list List snapshots at --db-path baseline delete --label LABEL Delete a snapshot at --db-path diff --baseline LABEL Compare a live run with a stored snapshot diff LABEL_A LABEL_B Compare two stored snapshots explain QUESTION_ID Rerun evaluation and show a question's requirements and missing evidence watch Poll the golden file and rerun after changes

docs.title: Common evaluation options
docs.text:
longprobe check --goldens tests/goldens.yaml --config longprobe.yaml
longprobe check --threshold 0.9 --top-k 10
longprobe check --tag critical --tag billing
longprobe check --include-drafts
longprobe check --output json
longprobe check --output github

Multiple tags require all specified tags. Empty input, no matching tags, and no approved selected questions fail rather than pass. --include-drafts does not allow a genuinely empty evaluation. Configuration/input errors fail even when fail_on_regression is false.

JSON output can still contain notices or command-specific trailing status text; a general machine-output cleanup is deferred. The default pytest adapter fixture also remains limited; supply your own adapter fixture. Explanations do not implement rank deltas or distance-drop analysis.

docs.title: Generation and capture
docs.text:
longprobe capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto
longprobe capture --questions-file questions.txt --match-mode id
longprobe generate ./documents --num-questions 20 --auto-capture
longprobe edit

Generate requires the optional generation dependencies and a configured provider/model. Auto-capture requires a retriever and saves drafts. Existing invalid/unreadable goldens fail preflight before LLM/retrieval calls and are never reset automatically.

Question-list export is a separate mode:

longprobe generate ./documents --output questions.yaml
longprobe generate ./documents --output questions.yaml --overwrite

The second command explicitly replaces an existing question-list output. --overwrite requires --output and cannot be combined with --auto-capture. --output and --auto-capture cannot be combined. Exported question lists need verified expected evidence before evaluation; they are not editable golden sets.

docs.title: Baselines and watch
docs.text:
longprobe baseline save --label latest
longprobe baseline list --db-path .longprobe/baselines.db
longprobe diff --baseline latest
longprobe watch --interval 2

Saving another label does not update latest. Baseline-save policy and historical comparison behavior are unchanged by this reliability patch. Watch runs only after a golden-file change, not immediately or on configuration/index changes. A failed watch iteration is reported and the watcher keeps waiting.

See configuration and recovery and the quick start.

docs.title: Golden Questions
docs.text: Golden questions are the foundation of LongProbe testing. They define what your RAG system should retrieve.

docs.title: What is a Golden Question?
docs.text:
A golden question consists of:

  • Question: The query to test
  • Required Chunks: Document chunks that must be retrieved
  • Match Mode: How to verify chunks (ID, text, or semantic)
  • Top-K: Number of results to retrieve
  • Tags: Optional metadata for organization

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
questions:
  - id: "q1"
    question: "What is the refund policy?"
    match_mode: "text"
    required_chunks:
      - "30-day money-back guarantee"
      - "full refund within 30 days"
    top_k: 5
    tags: ["policy", "critical"]

docs.title: Match Modes
docs.text: See Match Modes for detailed explanations.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start Small - Begin with 5-10 critical questions
  2. Be Specific - Test specific facts, not general topics
  3. Use Tags - Organize by importance or category
  4. Test Edge Cases - Include difficult queries
  5. Update Regularly - Add questions when bugs are found

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Match Modes - Understand matching strategies
  • CLI Reference - Run your tests

docs.title: Match Modes
docs.text: LongProbe supports three match modes for verifying retrieved chunks.

docs.title: ID Match
docs.text:
Exact string match on chunk/document IDs.

match_mode: "id"
required_chunks:
  - "doc_a_chunk_3"
  - "doc_b_chunk_7"

docs.title: Text Match
docs.text:
Case-insensitive substring matching.

match_mode: "text"
required_chunks:
  - "30-day money-back guarantee"

docs.title: Semantic Match
docs.text:
Word-frequency cosine similarity.

match_mode: "semantic"
semantic_threshold: 0.80
required_chunks:
  - "Only the CFO and CEO may authorize payments"

docs.title: Choosing a Match Mode
docs.text:
• ID: When you control chunk IDs
  • Text: For exact phrases
  • Semantic: When wording may vary

docs.title: LangChain Integration Guide
docs.text: LongProbe provides native, first-class integration with LangChain vector stores and retrievers. This guide explains how to connect LongProbe to your LangChain RAG pipelines to measure retrieval recall, detect missing document chunks, and prevent regressions in CI/CD.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
To use LongProbe with LangChain, install the [langchain] extra package:

pip install "longprobe[langchain]"

Or using uv:

uv add "longprobe[langchain]"

docs.title: Pattern A: Native Retriever Adapter (Recommended)
docs.text:
LongProbe automatically adapts any LangChain BaseRetriever or VectorStore (such as Chroma, FAISS, PGVector, Qdrant, or Pinecone).

When you wrap a LangChain retriever, LongProbe automatically extracts Document.page_content and Document.metadata to evaluate recall:

from langchain_community.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainAdapter

# 1. Initialize your existing LangChain vector store
vectorstore = Chroma(
    collection_name="corporate_docs",
    embedding_function=OpenAIEmbeddings(),
    persist_directory="./chroma_db",
)

# 2. Create a LangChain retriever
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})

# 3. Wrap with LongProbe LangChainAdapter
adapter = LangChainAdapter(retriever)

# 4. Run retrieval evaluation against Golden Questions
probe = LongProbe(
    adapter=adapter,
    goldens_path="goldens.yaml"
)

report = probe.run()
print(f"Overall Recall: {report.overall_recall:.1%}")
print(f"Pass Rate: {report.pass_rate:.1%}")

docs.title: How Chunk Extraction Works:
docs.text: When LongProbe queries a LangChain retriever: 1. retriever.invoke(query) (or get_relevant_documents) is called. 2. LongProbe extracts: * Text: doc.page_content $\rightarrow$ Mapped to text for ground-truth matching. * ID: doc.metadata.get("id") or doc.metadata.get("chunk_id") $\rightarrow$ Mapped to id for exact ID matching. * Metadata: Full doc.metadata dictionary. 3. LongProbe compares retrieved text/IDs against required ground-truth chunks using match_mode: text, match_mode: id, or match_mode: semantic.

docs.title: Pattern B: Custom LCEL Chain or Callable Wrapping
docs.text:
If your LangChain pipeline uses custom LCEL (LangChain Expression Language) runnables, RAG fusion, or multi-step chains, wrap the retrieval step in a lightweight Python callable:

from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import CustomAdapter

# Define a function that takes a query string and returns a list of chunk dicts
def langchain_rag_chain_retriever(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
    # Invoke your custom LangChain retriever or chain
    docs = retriever.invoke(query)

    return [
        {
            "id": doc.metadata.get("chunk_id", f"doc_{i}"),
            "text": doc.page_content,
            "metadata": doc.metadata,
        }
        for i, doc in enumerate(docs[:top_k])
    ]

# Wrap in CustomAdapter
adapter = CustomAdapter(retrieval_fn=langchain_rag_chain_retriever)

probe = LongProbe(adapter=adapter, goldens_path="goldens.yaml")
report = probe.run()

docs.title: 3. End-to-End Walkthrough
docs.text:
Here is a complete, runnable example using LangChain document chunking and vector storage:

from langchain_community.document_loaders import TextLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_community.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainAdapter

# Step 1: Ingest & Chunk Documents with LangChain
loader = TextLoader("refund_policy.txt")
documents = loader.load()

text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
chunks = text_splitter.split_documents(documents)

# Step 2: Index Chunks into VectorStore
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(
    documents=chunks,
    embedding=OpenAIEmbeddings(),
    collection_name="policy_docs"
)

# Step 3: Run LongProbe Quality Check
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})
adapter = LangChainAdapter(retriever)

probe = LongProbe(adapter=adapter, goldens_path="goldens.yaml")
report = probe.run()

# Step 4: Check Results & Baseline
if report.overall_recall < 0.85:
    print("⚠️ Quality Gate Warning: Retrieval recall below 85%!")
else:
    print("✅ Quality Gate Passed!")

docs.title: 4. Continuous Integration & Pytest
docs.text:
Add LangChain regression checks directly to your test suite (pytest):

import pytest
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainAdapter

def test_langchain_retrieval_quality(my_langchain_retriever):
    adapter = LangChainAdapter(my_langchain_retriever)
    probe = LongProbe(adapter=adapter, goldens_path="goldens.yaml")

    report = probe.run()

    # Assert recall threshold in CI/CD
    assert report.overall_recall >= 0.85, f"Retrieval recall dropped to {report.overall_recall:.1%}"

Run in terminal: 

uv run pytest tests/test_rag_pipeline.py

docs.title: 5. Best Practices for LangChain Pipelines
docs.text:
1. Include Chunk IDs in Metadata: When using LangChain text splitters, add a unique ID to doc.metadata["id"] or doc.metadata["chunk_id"]. This allows match_mode: id evaluation in LongProbe.
  2. Tune search_kwargs={"k": ...}: Ensure k matches the top_k specified in your goldens.yaml questions.
  3. Test Text Splitter Changes: Whenever you adjust chunk_size or chunk_overlap in LangChain, run longprobe check to ensure key information isn't split across chunk boundaries.

docs.title: v0.1.3 — Restore Basic Reliability
docs.text: Status: implemented locally; not tagged, published, or pushed. Verification date: October 16, 2026. Proposed release deadline: October 23, 2026 (Asia/Karachi).

docs.title: Delivered changes
docs.text:
Requirement Implementation REL-01: Startup Valid Python source, base-only public imports/help without service calls, lazy optional SDKs, and actionable missing-SDK errors REL-02: Version pyproject.toml is authoritative; runtime version comes from installed distribution metadata; wheel/source metadata identify 0.1.3 REL-03: Configuration Strict shapes/types/ranges, contextual active-provider validation, safe YAML errors, no CLI fallback, and preserved deliberate Python defaults REL-04: Empty evaluation Zero evaluated questions fail across CLI/scorer/facade; empty authoring still works; failed reruns invalidate previous reports REL-05: Files Candidate validation, preflight before generation, atomic per-file writes, permission preservation, explicit replacement, and unchanged existing data on tested ordinary failures REL-06: Documentation Corrected setup/configuration/CLI examples, local HTTP fixture, recovery instructions, and known limitations

init copies hardcoded examples; it does not create questions from documents or embeddings. Use verified manual cases, capture, or document-based generation followed by review. See the quick start.

docs.title: Compatibility changes
docs.text:
• Requires Python 3.11 or newer. Python 3.10 support was removed after the initial reliability verification.

  • Invalid CLI settings no longer silently become defaults. Correct the reported field or selected path.

  • No approved/matching questions means a failed evaluation, even when quality-failure exit behavior is disabled.
  • Python users supplying an adapter may still omit the conventional default configuration file; custom missing files and broken links fail.
  • Question-list replacement uses generate --output PATH --overwrite. Output and auto-capture modes cannot be combined.
  • Invalid existing auto-capture goldens must be repaired or a new destination selected. They are never reset automatically.
  • Use an editable installation for source development; runtime version resolution requires installed distribution metadata.
  • No baseline database/schema migration is required.

docs.title: Verification results
docs.text:
The following results are local runs, not GitHub-hosted CI results:

Environment/check Result Historical Python 3.10.21 run, before the minimum-version change 270 passed; 15 optional Chroma cases skipped Python 3.11.16, full collected suite with integration enabled 270 passed; 15 optional Chroma cases skipped Python 3.12.14, full collected suite with integration enabled 270 passed; 15 optional Chroma cases skipped Source and changed/new test/example/helper lint Passed Strict MkDocs build Passed; existing README/index conflict and broken placeholder links corrected Locked Python 3.12 development sync Passed; Python 3.10-only dependency branches removed Wheel and source archive build Passed Clean base-only wheel installation outside checkout Passed Installed CLI local HTTP check → baseline → diff Passed; intentional empty-tag evaluation failed as expected Startup network/project-data side effects None observed under the guarded smoke test Runtime/distribution/source-archive version comparison 0.1.3 throughout Rebuilt package minimum and installer rejection Requires-Python: >=3.11; Python 3.10 installation rejected

The Chroma SDK was not installed in these environments. Its 15 optional integration cases were explicitly skipped by their existing fixture. Live cloud backends, paid question generation, Windows/macOS permissions, and the full all-extras CI environment were not exercised. GitHub Actions must still run after the user pushes.

docs.title: Acceptance traceability
docs.text:
Test IDs refer to the v0.1.3 requirements document in the planning workspace.

Cases Evidence in the repository T-01/T-02 tests/unit/test_startup.py: guarded imports/help, source syntax, and missing SDKs for all five optional adapter families T-03 Installed runtime metadata test plus examples/verify_v013_release.py and clean artifact verification T-04–T-08 tests/unit/test_config.py: load/default rules, invalid scalar/section values, active/inactive credentials, typed objects, and secret sentinels T-09–T-12 tests/unit/test_empty_evaluation.py and scorer tests: selection failure, draft inclusion, direct scorer, stale reports, and watch continuation T-13/T-14 tests/unit/test_cli_file_safety.py: invalid/unreadable preflight, zero paid calls, merge preservation, new drafts T-15/T-16 tests/unit/test_file_safety.py: serialization, stream write/flush, sync and replacement failure injection; Unicode, nested paths, cleanup, read-only and symbolic-link handling T-17–T-19 CLI file-safety tests: initialization preservation/force, export overwrite rules, and zero-capture byte preservation T-20 tests/integration/test_reliability_workflow.py: local HTTP capture → approval → check → baseline → diff, plus regression and preservation paths

Atomic saves are scoped to a single regular-file writer. Tests cover POSIX mode preservation and injected permission failures; no claim is made that every ACL/filesystem/power-loss condition has been exercised.

docs.title: Reproducing the checks
docs.text:
From the project root:

uv sync --locked --dev --python 3.12
uv run pytest tests/ --run-integration -q
uv run ruff check src/
uv build

The local HTTP integration requires permission to bind a localhost socket. Base installation and artifact verification should run separately from a development environment:

uv venv /tmp/longprobe-wheel-check --python 3.12
uv pip install --python /tmp/longprobe-wheel-check/bin/python dist/longprobe-0.1.3-py3-none-any.whl
/tmp/longprobe-wheel-check/bin/python -I examples/verify_v013_release.py

The verification script uses the installed wheel rather than the editable checkout, confirms optional SDKs/test dependencies are absent, starts the synthetic HTTP example, and prints artifact SHA-256 hashes. Keep the wheel environment base-only. Supported-version tests run on Python 3.11 and 3.12. The earlier Python 3.10 result is historical and does not indicate current support.

docs.title: Release identity and disposition
docs.text:
Read-only checks on October 16, 2026 returned PyPI versions 0.1.0 and 0.1.1, and public repository tags v0.1.0 and v0.1.1. Sources: PyPI metadata, GitHub tags API. Version availability must be rechecked before tagging/publishing because public state can change.

The syntax-breaking URL was a pre-existing uncommitted addition in this local checkout. It was preserved in a temporary backup and removed, restoring the tracked valid adapter source. No unrelated initial working-tree changes were present.

Local disposition: implementation checks pass for the specified reliability scope. Publication remains a maintainer action after remote CI and release review. No push, tag creation, or package publication was performed.

docs.title: Remaining limitations
docs.text:
• Normal evaluation does not wire embedder settings into vector-only backends. Pinecone/Qdrant text-question integration remains deferred.
  • Semantic matching is word-frequency similarity, not neural embedding matching.
  • The default pytest adapter fixture still needs an override.
  • Baseline-save quality policies differ between CLI/Python; baseline compatibility and equal-recall evidence-change detection are unchanged.
  • JSON stdout may still include notices/trailing command output; general cleanup is deferred.
  • Explain does not calculate rank/score deltas. Watch still reacts only to golden-file changes.
  • No automatically verified ground truth is promised for LLM-generated/captured evidence; review drafts before approval.
